title: The Fox and the Stork

full_text:
The fox, always fond of mischievous pranks at the expense of others, invited his neighbor the Stork to dine with him at his den. The polite bird accepted the invitation with gracious courtesy, arriving at the appointed hour with a keen appetite.

The fox brought out dinner with a mocking grin: a thin, aromatic broth served in shallow earthenware saucers. The fox lapped up his soup in seconds with his broad tongue, but the poor Stork, with her long, slender bill, could only peck uselessly at the flat plate, wetting the very tip of her beak while the broth slipped away.

"You do not eat, neighbor Stork!" chuckled the deceitful fox. "Is the soup not spiced to your liking?"

"Do not concern yourself, friend," replied the dignified Stork politely. "I have enjoyed the visit immensely. In return, I invite you to dine with me at my nest tomorrow evening."

The following evening, the hungry fox arrived at the Stork's dwelling, eager for a free feast. The Stork welcomed him and brought out dinner: a savory stew of tender minced meat and rich gravy, served inside tall, narrow-necked glass jars with slender bases.

The Stork inserted her long bill easily into the jar, feasting delicately and savoring every mouthful. The fox, unable to squeeze his broad snout through the narrow glass neck, could only lick the rim in ravenous misery while his stomach growled in humiliation.

Seeing the fox's furious embarrassment, the Stork smiled calmly and said: "Do not grumble, friend Fox. He who plays cruel tricks upon his guests must not complain when the same hospitality is returned to him!"
moral: One bad turn deserves another; treat guests as you wish to be treated yourself.
